items.q: Sales of home blood-pressure monitors ______ after the ministry's warning about undiagnosed hypertension, rising fivefold in a single month.
items.vi: Doanh số máy đo huyết áp tại nhà tăng vọt sau cảnh báo của bộ y tế về tình trạng cao huyết áp chưa được chẩn đoán, tăng gấp năm lần chỉ trong một tháng.
items.explanation: Skyrocket = rise extremely fast, the only verb that matches rising fivefold in a single month. ✗ dwindled — shrink slowly, the opposite direction; ✗ fluctuated — rise and fall repeatedly, not one steady jump; ✗ stagnated — stop growing, contradicted by a fivefold rise.

items.q: Persuading teenagers to switch off location sharing has proved ______ for privacy campaigners, who report that fewer than one in ten has done so.
items.vi: Việc thuyết phục thanh thiếu niên tắt chia sẻ vị trí đã tỏ ra là một cuộc chiến gian nan đối với các nhà vận động về quyền riêng tư, những người cho biết chưa tới một phần mười các em làm vậy.
items.explanation: An uphill battle = a struggle that is very hard to win, which fewer than one in ten has done so shows. ✗ a foregone conclusion — a result certain in advance, but the campaign is failing; ✗ a blessing in disguise — hidden good luck, yet nothing good has come of it; ✗ a red herring — a misleading clue, which a persuasion effort cannot be.

items.q: Facial recognition in shopping centres ______ a serious threat to the anonymity that city life once guaranteed.
items.vi: Công nghệ nhận diện khuôn mặt ở các trung tâm mua sắm đặt ra mối đe dọa nghiêm trọng đối với sự ẩn danh mà đời sống đô thị từng bảo đảm.
items.explanation: The verb that goes with threat (and risk, danger, problem) is pose: 'pose a serious threat' = be a danger to something. ✗ makes — 'make a threat' = say you will harm someone, not be a danger; ✗ does — never collocates with 'threat'; ✗ puts — needs a place ('put at risk'), not 'a threat'.

items.q: Not until a journalist published the leaked database ______ that millions of accounts had been exposed.
items.vi: Mãi đến khi một nhà báo công bố cơ sở dữ liệu bị rò rỉ, công ty mới thừa nhận rằng hàng triệu tài khoản đã bị lộ.
items.explanation: A fronted Not until clause forces inversion in the main clause: auxiliary + subject + bare verb, did the company admit. ✗ the company admitted — no inversion after the negative opener; ✗ had the company admitted — inverted, but past perfect puts the admission before the publishing, the wrong order; ✗ the company did admit — 'did' is there but the subject must follow it.

items.q: The laboratory will gradually ______ its vaccine production over the next six months rather than halt it overnight.
items.vi: Phòng thí nghiệm sẽ dần thu hẹp hoạt động sản xuất vắc-xin trong sáu tháng tới thay vì dừng đột ngột.
items.explanation: Wind down = reduce an activity gradually before ending it, contrasted with rather than halt it overnight. ✗ wind up — bring to a complete end / close a company, the sudden halt the sentence rejects; ✗ wear down — exhaust or erode (resistance, patience), not scale back production; ✗ tone down — make less forceful (language, colours), not reduce output.

items.q: Public enthusiasm for the fitness app began to ______ once users discovered how much location data it had been collecting.
items.vi: Sự hào hứng của công chúng với ứng dụng thể dục bắt đầu nguội dần khi người dùng phát hiện nó đã thu thập bao nhiêu dữ liệu vị trí.
items.explanation: Wane = decrease gradually in strength, the natural result of discovered how much location data it had been collecting. ✗ accelerate — speed up or increase, the wrong direction after a scandal; ✗ rebound — recover after a fall, but there has been no fall yet; ✗ escalate — grow more intense (conflicts, prices), not lose strength.

items.q: After a decade of lawsuits, the two chip makers agreed to ______ the ______ and pool their patents on medical sensors.
items.vi: Sau một thập kỷ kiện tụng, hai hãng sản xuất chip đồng ý gác lại hiềm khích và gộp chung các bằng sáng chế về cảm biến y tế.
items.explanation: Bury the hatchet = end a long quarrel and make peace, the meaning behind a decade of lawsuits ending in pooled patents. ✗ bite the bullet — accept something painful bravely, no peace-making; ✗ break the ice — ease awkwardness at a first meeting, not after ten years of conflict; ✗ call the shots — be the one in control, not agree with a rival.

items.q: The patient ______ the tablets on an empty stomach, or she would not be feeling this nauseous now.
items.vi: Bệnh nhân hẳn đã uống thuốc lúc bụng đói, nếu không thì giờ cô ấy đã không buồn nôn đến thế.
items.explanation: Would not be feeling this nauseous now is present evidence, so the speaker draws a confident deduction about the past: must have taken. ✗ can't have taken — the opposite deduction ('surely did not'), which could not cause the nausea; ✗ should have taken — criticism of a failure to act, but she did take them; ✗ needn't have taken — it was unnecessary, which explains no cause.

items.q: Researchers who blame screen time alone for teenage insomnia may be ______, since the latest data point to caffeine as the stronger factor.
options: putting the cart before the horse
items.vi: Các nhà nghiên cứu chỉ đổ lỗi cho thời gian dùng màn hình gây mất ngủ ở tuổi teen có lẽ đang nhắm sai hướng, vì dữ liệu mới nhất cho thấy caffeine là yếu tố mạnh hơn.
items.explanation: Bark up the wrong tree = pursue a mistaken explanation or target, which caffeine as the stronger factor implies about blaming screens. ✗ beat around the bush — avoid saying something directly, but the researchers state their view plainly; ✗ jump on the bandwagon — follow a popular trend, no fashion is mentioned; ✗ put the cart before the horse — do things in the wrong order, not blame the wrong cause.

items.q: Rural clinics have been left to ______ the burden of the vaccination drive while city hospitals receive most of the extra funding.
items.vi: Các phòng khám nông thôn bị bỏ mặc gánh vác gánh nặng của chiến dịch tiêm chủng, trong khi các bệnh viện thành phố nhận phần lớn khoản kinh phí bổ sung.
items.explanation: Taking on a heavy responsibility is shoulder the burden (also shoulder the cost / the blame), so the clinics carry the load alone. ✗ foot — only 'foot the bill' (pay); ✗ head — lead a committee, a list or a team, not carry a burden; ✗ hand — needs a particle ('hand over / out') and means give, not carry.

items.q: It is vital that the lead researcher ______ the safety briefing in person before the trial resumes.
items.vi: Điều thiết yếu là trưởng nhóm nghiên cứu phải trực tiếp tham dự buổi phổ biến an toàn trước khi thử nghiệm được nối lại.
items.explanation: After It is vital that (also essential, important, necessary) the that-clause takes the base-form subjunctive whatever the subject: the researcher attend. ✗ attended — past tense, but the briefing is a future requirement; ✗ attending — not a finite verb, so the clause has no main verb; ✗ will attend — a plain future prediction, which the subjunctive pattern does not allow.

items.q: Shares in the social network ______ by a fifth in a single afternoon after regulators announced a privacy investigation.
items.vi: Cổ phiếu của mạng xã hội này lao dốc một phần năm chỉ trong một buổi chiều sau khi cơ quan quản lý công bố cuộc điều tra về quyền riêng tư.
items.explanation: Tumble = fall suddenly and steeply, matching by a fifth in a single afternoon. ✗ dwindled — a slow, gradual shrinking, not a one-afternoon crash; ✗ crept — moved very slowly, the opposite of a sudden drop; ✗ hovered — stayed roughly level, so it cannot take 'by a fifth'.

items.q: ______ carefully a hospital encrypts its records, a single careless password can undo the whole effort.
items.vi: Dù một bệnh viện mã hóa hồ sơ cẩn thận đến đâu, chỉ một mật khẩu bất cẩn cũng có thể làm đổ sông đổ biển toàn bộ nỗ lực.
items.explanation: The blank is followed directly by the adverb carefully, so the concessive opener must be No matter how (= however carefully). ✗ Whatever — must be followed by a noun ('whatever precautions'), not an adverb; ✗ Even though — introduces a full clause beginning with the subject ('even though a hospital encrypts'); ✗ In spite of — a preposition, so it needs a noun phrase, not 'carefully ... encrypts'.

items.q: Using the phone's metadata, investigators were able to ______ the exact building from which the stolen files had been uploaded.
items.vi: Nhờ siêu dữ liệu của chiếc điện thoại, các điều tra viên đã khoanh vùng được chính xác tòa nhà nơi các tệp bị đánh cắp đã được tải lên.
items.explanation: Zero in on = identify and focus precisely on a target, the only option with the correct particle. ✗ zoom in at — the phrase is 'zoom in on'; ✗ home in to — the phrase is 'home in on'; ✗ close in at — the phrase is 'close in on'. All three verbs would fit in meaning, but each pairs only with 'on'.

items.q: At the hearing, the journalist asked the chief executive ______ the company had ever sold its users' location history to advertisers.
items.vi: Tại phiên điều trần, nhà báo hỏi vị tổng giám đốc liệu công ty có bao giờ bán lịch sử vị trí của người dùng cho các nhà quảng cáo hay không.
items.explanation: Asked ... the company had ever sold is a reported yes/no question, so it is introduced by whether (or 'if') with statement word order. ✗ that — reports a statement, not a question; ✗ what — would need a missing object, but 'sold its users' location history' is already complete; ✗ did — direct-question order, impossible inside reported speech.

items.q: The surgeon is not one to ______, but her transplant team's survival figures speak for themselves.
items.vi: Vị bác sĩ phẫu thuật không phải người thích khoe khoang, nhưng con số tỷ lệ sống sót của đội ghép tạng của bà đã tự nói lên tất cả.
items.explanation: Blow your own trumpet = boast about your achievements, which contrasts with the figures that speak for themselves. ✗ blow hot and cold — keep changing your mind, nothing to do with modesty; ✗ blow the whistle — expose wrongdoing, none is mentioned; ✗ blow her top — lose her temper, unrelated to praise.

items.q: Older users seem resigned to ______ tracked wherever they go online, whereas teenagers are increasingly fighting back.
items.vi: Người dùng lớn tuổi dường như cam chịu việc bị theo dõi ở bất cứ đâu họ lên mạng, trong khi thanh thiếu niên ngày càng phản kháng.
items.explanation: In resigned to the 'to' is a preposition (like 'used to', 'look forward to', 'object to'), so it is followed by a gerund: being tracked. ✗ be — a bare infinitive cannot follow a preposition; ✗ to be — would give 'to to be', a doubled 'to'; ✗ been — a past participle needs 'have / has' before it.

items.q: The probe is now ______ towards Jupiter at almost 200,000 kilometres an hour, faster than any craft before it.
items.vi: Tàu thăm dò hiện đang lao về phía Sao Mộc với tốc độ gần 200.000 km/giờ, nhanh hơn bất kỳ con tàu nào trước đó.
items.explanation: Hurtle = move at very great speed, often out of control, fitting almost 200,000 kilometres an hour. ✗ drifting — moving slowly with no power or direction; ✗ dawdling — moving slowly and lazily, wasting time; ✗ meandering — following a slow, winding path. All three describe slowness, the opposite of the clue.

items.q: ______ a surge in counterfeit medicines, the health ministry has ordered every pharmacy to scan a barcode on each pack it sells.
items.vi: Trước tình trạng thuốc giả gia tăng, bộ y tế đã yêu cầu mọi hiệu thuốc quét mã vạch trên từng hộp thuốc bán ra.
items.explanation: The ministry was moved to act by the surge, so a past participle with passive meaning is needed: Prompted by a surge = because it was prompted by one. ✗ Prompting by — an active participle makes the ministry the cause, leaving 'by' with nothing to attach to; ✗ Having prompted by — an active perfect participle, the same wrong direction; ✗ To prompt by — an infinitive of purpose, not a participle clause, and the ministry did not act in order to prompt.

items.q: Even a ______ smoker who quits at fifty regains several years of life expectancy, the study concludes.
items.vi: Ngay cả một người nghiện thuốc nặng bỏ thuốc ở tuổi năm mươi cũng lấy lại được vài năm tuổi thọ, nghiên cứu kết luận.
items.explanation: Someone who smokes a great deal is a heavy smoker (likewise a heavy drinker, heavy traffic, heavy rain): 'heavy' marks large quantity. ✗ strong — describes the cigarette or its taste, not the person; ✗ hard — 'a hard worker' exists, but 'hard smoker' is not a collocation; ✗ big — used in 'a big eater / big spender', not with 'smoker'.

items.q: It ______ out that the clinic had been ______ patient records on an unsecured server for almost three years.
items.vi: Hóa ra phòng khám đã lưu trữ hồ sơ bệnh nhân trên một máy chủ không được bảo mật trong gần ba năm.
items.explanation: It turned out that = it was discovered that; and after had been the past perfect continuous needs the -ing form, storing. ✗ ended / to store — 'end out' does not exist and 'had been to store' is meaningless; ✗ worked / stored — 'it worked out that' is not used for discovering a fact, and 'had been stored patient records' leaves no object slot; ✗ made / storing — 'make out that' means to pretend, not to discover.

items.q: The telehealth start-up expects to ______ by next spring, once subscription income finally covers its server costs.
items.vi: Công ty khởi nghiệp y tế từ xa dự kiến sẽ hòa vốn vào mùa xuân tới, khi thu nhập từ thuê bao cuối cùng bù đắp được chi phí máy chủ.
items.explanation: Break even = make neither a profit nor a loss, exactly what income finally covers its server costs describes. ✗ break ground — start building on a site, unrelated to money; ✗ break ranks — stop supporting your own group; ✗ break the bank — cost far too much, the opposite of covering costs.

items.q: ______ leaks a patient's records, even unintentionally, now faces a fine of up to a year's salary under the new law.
items.vi: Bất kỳ ai làm rò rỉ hồ sơ bệnh nhân, dù vô ý, giờ đây đều đối mặt với khoản phạt lên tới một năm lương theo luật mới.
items.explanation: Whoever = any person who; it is the subject of leaks (and of 'faces'), so the subject form is needed. ✗ Whomever — object form, but the pronoun performs the verb 'leaks'; ✗ Whichever — a choice among a known set of things, not an unknown person; ✗ Whom — object form, and a plain relative cannot open a sentence with no antecedent.

items.q: Life expectancy in the region has ______ at around 72 for a decade, despite heavy investment in new hospitals.
items.vi: Tuổi thọ trung bình ở khu vực này đã chững lại ở mức khoảng 72 suốt một thập kỷ, bất chấp đầu tư mạnh vào các bệnh viện mới.
items.explanation: Plateau = stop rising and stay level, which at around 72 for a decade and 'despite heavy investment' both signal. ✗ rocketed — shot up fast, but the figure has not moved; ✗ rebounded — recovered after a fall, and no fall is mentioned; ✗ dipped — fell briefly, which cannot be followed by 'at around 72 for a decade'.

items.q: Nobody expected the vaccine to clear the regulator's review this quickly, ______?
items.vi: Không ai ngờ vắc-xin lại vượt qua đợt xét duyệt của cơ quan quản lý nhanh đến thế, phải không?
items.explanation: Nobody makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive, and indefinite person subjects (nobody, everyone, someone) take they: did they. ✗ didn't they — a negative tag after a negative statement; ✗ did it — 'it' would refer to the vaccine, but the subject is 'nobody'; ✗ wasn't it — wrong auxiliary ('expected' needs 'did') and wrong pronoun.
